content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines supporting three product teams and has improved pipeline speed and test reliability through parallelisation, caching and ephemeral environments. Hands-on experience with Docker, Helm and a shared Kubernetes cluster, plus Python and Bash tooling. Seeking to move into a DevOps or platform engineering role full time.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and moving end-to-end tests to on-demand ephemeral environments.
- Built ephemeral test environments for each merge request using Docker Compose, later adopting Helm charts on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to under 1%.
- Developed Bash and Python tooling to seed test data into PostgreSQL.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications for client projects.
- Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and Infrastructure: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Programming and Scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Systems and Monitoring: Linux, Git, PostgreSQL, Grafana (dashboards for test metrics)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, concise and professional CV with strong quantified achievements. The most persuasive evidence is the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to under 1%, ownership of GitLab CI for three product teams, and the use of Docker, Helm and Kubernetes for ephemeral environments. The structure is easy to scan and the career progression toward test infrastructure is credible. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a strong QA/test-infrastructure profile but only a partial match for a cloud infrastructure and DevOps contractor role. The statement that the candidate is seeking to move into DevOps is honest, but it also makes the CV read as a transition profile rather than as an established infrastructure engineer.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, standard bullets and readable keyword groupings, so it should parse well in most ATS platforms. Relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, Python, Bash, Linux, PostgreSQL and Grafana are present. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate for this specific role: the document is likely to be recognized as relevant to CI/CD, test infrastructure and containerized environments, but likely to rank below candidates with explicit Terraform, Terragrunt, AWS, cloud infrastructure, networking, mTLS, SSL/TLS, security and systems architecture experience. Do not add those terms unless supported by the candidate's actual background.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows meaningful hands-on infrastructure-related work through CI/CD ownership, build and test environments, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes and pipeline optimization. It also demonstrates analytical thinking through measurable reliability and performance improvements, and it shows some technical ownership through responsibility for pipelines supporting three product teams. However, the candidate's material does not establish the role's core cloud infrastructure requirements: Terraform/Terragrunt, AWS or another major cloud, networking including mTLS and SSL/TLS, practical security, formal systems architecture/design, remote-device or IoT integration, or virtual-machine experience. The document also does not demonstrate leading technical proposals and bringing external or cross-functional stakeholders along. Java is present only as test code, not as a JVM backend or full-stack background. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be repaired through wording. The CV is strongest for the CI/CD, test-platform and containerized-environment aspects of the role.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the CV does not contain apparent unsupported skills or experience when checked against the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence, "Seeking to move into a DevOps or platform engineering role full time," with a more evidence-led positioning statement such as: "Targeting DevOps and platform engineering work focused on CI/CD, containerized test environments and reliable developer tooling." This keeps the career direction truthful while emphasizing the infrastructure capabilities already demonstrated rather than foregrounding the transition.
2. In the headline, consider changing "QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure" to "QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD, Containers & Test Infrastructure." The added terms are directly supported by the Docker, Docker Compose, Helm and Kubernetes experience and improve keyword alignment without implying unsupported cloud or Terraform experience.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change the category heading "CI/CD and Infrastructure" to "CI/CD, Containers and Test Infrastructure." Keep the existing tools unchanged. This more accurately describes the documented experience and avoids suggesting that the candidate has broader cloud infrastructure experience than the CV supports.
4. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, revise the first bullet to make the operational scope more explicit while remaining truthful: "Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, artifact publishing and pipeline reliability." Only retain the final phrase if pipeline reliability is genuinely part of the responsibility; the existing quantified flaky-test and pipeline-speed results support that context.
